Deep_Keeled_Swimming_Tail.description: An incredibly deep, laterally compressed tail featuring a prominent upper and lower fleshy fin margin. It provides phenomenal forward thrust during sinusoidal swimming motions in dense marsh water.

Prehensile_Arboreal_Tail.description: A highly muscular, incredibly flexible tail capable of independently grasping and tightly coiling around slick branches. It functions perfectly as an indispensable fifth limb during precarious high-canopy navigation.

Aposematic_Lure_Tail.description: The tip of the tail is dramatically colored in blazing reds or yellows and twitches erratically, perfectly mimicking a struggling worm. It effortlessly draws completely oblivious prey directly into striking range of the jaws.

Autotomic_Decoy_Tail.description: A tail featuring specialized fracture planes in the vertebrae. When grabbed by a predator, the tail instantly severs itself autonomously, writhing violently on the ground to serve as a high-value biological decoy while the entity escapes.

Glandular_Fat_Storage_Tail.description: An immensely swollen, absurdly thick tail packed solidly with dense lipid reserves. It guarantees absolute survival during multi-year subterranean droughts, but severely hampers terrestrial running speed.

Serrated_Comb_Tail.description: The dorsal ridge of the tail features a series of intensely sharp, heavily keratinized spines. Sweeping the tail violently side-to-side can inflict profound, lacerating wounds on pursuing aquatic predators.

Rudder_Like_Flattened_Tail.description: A tail aggressively flattened top-to-bottom like a beaver's. Rather than thrust, it serves primarily as an exceptional biological rudder for tight, high-speed underwater hairpin turns.

Toxic_Secretion_Caudal_Glands.description: The entire length of the tail is densely packed with specialized exocrine glands. When threatened, the entity assumes a defensive posture and violently secretes a blinding, mucosal neurotoxin directly from its tail.

Vestigial_Stump_Tail.description: An evolutionary remnant representing the total loss of a true tail (anurans). The lack of trailing biomass slightly improves aerodynamic leaping distance and denies predators an easy grasping point.

Dorsal_Respiratory_Fin_Tail.description: A phenomenally developed tail fin consisting almost entirely of highly vascularized, exposed capillary beds. Evolved for oxygen-poor stagnant water, the tail itself actively pulls oxygen directly from the surrounding muck.
